content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the first 5–10 days post-spike, then corrects downward — suggest smoothing or lagged momentum adjustment.
- Shows strong mean reversion bias: forecasts drift toward historical averages too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Underestimates downward trends in low-price regimes (e.g., below 65) — model lacks sensitivity to price floor behavior.
- Overestimates upward momentum in high-price regimes — fails to cap upside potential after peaks.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 10 days of the 30-day window — model reacts too slowly to recent price changes.
- When true price drops sharply, model fails to adjust downward quickly — exhibits lagged correction.
- Model tends to overfit recent volatility — forecasts react too strongly to short-term noise, especially in 30-day window.
